cases.name: real-format-225-shaped-blocks-not-mirrored
cases._note: #662 BLOCKER exemplar — the live #225 body shape. 'Blocks: #213' is the RECIPROCAL (current blocks #213, NOT blocked-by #213); the defect mirrored it as blocked-by(225<-213), inverting the edge. 'Relates to:' targets are non-blocking. Nothing is mirror-eligible; to_add MUST be empty so no false native dependency is written.

cases.name: unlabelled-prose-section-mirrors-nothing
cases._note: Prose-attribution defect. A Dependencies section of free-form sentences ending in an epic reference. Pre-fix the whole section fell through the legacy bare-ref shim and planned the parent epic as a native blocker, while missing every real edge. Prose asserts no direction, so nothing is mirror-eligible.
cases.body:
### Dependencies

**Gated on** the host-decision **spike** and on the instrumentation stories (emit autonomous seams; stable join-key + emission gate). Composes the coverage-scorecard **task**. Part of epic **#1189**.

### Acceptance Criteria

cases.name: epic-ref-trailing-a-labelled-blocked-by-segment
cases._note: The labelled-body variant, and the worse case: a CORRECT `Blocked by:` label plus a trailing epic reference. Segments run to the next RECOGNIZED label, so pre-fix the epic was swallowed by the still-open Blocked by: segment and a well-formed body ALSO produced a false blocker. Authoring discipline alone could not avoid this; the epic label is required independently of the prose rule.
cases.body:
### Dependencies
Blocked by: #4024, #4025, #4026
Part of epic **#1189**.

cases.name: prose-refs-reported-as-unattributed
cases._note: Real dependencies stated only in prose: nothing is mirrored (no direction asserted) but the refs are REPORTED rather than dropped in silence, so the author can relabel them under `Blocked by:`. Reporting beats both alternatives — inventing an edge, or discarding the intent wordlessly.
cases.body:
### Dependencies
Gated on the host-decision spike #4024 and the instrumentation work in #4025.

cases.name: directional-heading-confers-direction-on-prose
cases._note: Guards against over-correction. `### Depends on` states the direction in the heading, so prose beneath it IS a real blocked-by list. The prose rule must suppress only genuinely directionless runs; an ambiguous `### Dependencies` heading over the same sentence confers nothing (see the paired negative case).
cases.body:
### Depends on
Needs the parser work in #201 to land first.

cases.name: ambiguous-heading-over-identical-prose-confers-nothing
cases._note: Paired negative for the directional-heading case: byte-identical prose under the ambiguous `### Dependencies` container yields no edge, and the ref surfaces as unattributed. The heading is the only difference, which is what makes the pair a control.
